Less paperwork. More progress.

ACCESSUG.SCH brings key school workflows together: school setup, student and staff records, classes and subjects, attendance, assessments and results, fee tracking, communication, and role-based portals.

Organise school profiles, classes, academic terms, subjects and essential settings from one place.

Built for local realities

Designed for schools where connectivity can be unreliable. The product vision puts practical access first.

Privacy by design

Every role has a purpose. Every record needs protection.

ACCESSUG.SCH uses a structured data model and is built around school-level access and clear user roles.

Security is part of the foundation.

Row-Level Security (RLS) policies help limit which records a user can access. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) helps keep each portal focused on the tasks that belong to that role. Policies should be reviewed and tested as the platform evolves.

⌑

Row-Level Security (RLS)

Database policies can restrict access to school and user records instead of relying only on interface rules.

♙

Role-Based Access Control

Separate experiences for administrators, teachers, students and parents help keep work relevant to each user.

▣

Structured school records

Schools, profiles, classes, attendance, assessments, reports and fee records are organised into related data areas.

↻

Account setup & sign-in

Account provisioning and identifier-based sign-in workflows support a practical onboarding experience.

Simple onboarding

Start with the right identity.

Clear account setup helps users get into the right school space from day one.

＋

First-time provisioning

New users complete an account setup flow and choose a unique username. Use 3–40 characters. Letters, numbers, periods, underscores and hyphens are supported by the current username rule.

e.g. teacher-jk · 3–40 characters
↪

Flexible sign-in

Identifier-based login is designed to accept a username, email address or phone number, alongside the user's sign-in credentials.

Username / Email / Phone
